name: Cloudflare Pages
limits: Free plan: 500 builds/month, 1 concurrent build, 20-minute build timeout, 100 custom domains per project. Pages Functions share the Workers Free quota of 100,000 requests/day; static asset requests are free and unlimited.
notes: Best all-round static host: unlimited bandwidth, global CDN, preview deployments, Git or direct upload. Projects can be created without a card.

name: GitHub Pages
limits: Public repository required on GitHub Free. Published site max 1 GB, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, 10 builds/hour soft limit (bypass with Actions), 10-minute deploy timeout. No server-side code, and commercial or SaaS sites are not allowed.
notes: Best for portfolios, documentation and project pages. Custom domains and HTTPS are free, and GitHub Actions can build any static framework.

name: GitLab Pages
limits: Maximum site size is 1 GB on GitLab.com, with up to 150 custom domains per site and 200,000 file entries. Sites build through CI/CD pipelines, so they consume shared runner minutes. Static files only.
notes: Good if your code already lives on GitLab. Custom domains and Let's Encrypt certificates are free; deploy with a .gitlab-ci.yml pipeline.

name: Codeberg Pages
limits: Static files only. Deploys go through a webhook or Forgejo Actions; custom domains require DNS TXT authorization. The legacy Pages v2 server shuts down on 31 December 2026, so new sites must use git-pages.
notes: Non-profit, privacy-focused host with no ads or tracking. Great for open-source project sites; custom domains and HTTPS are supported.

name: Netlify
limits: Free plan uses 300 credits/month: production deploy 15 credits, bandwidth 20 credits/GB, requests 2 credits per 10k, compute 10 credits per GB-hour. One concurrent build. When credits run out, projects pause until the next cycle. Older free accounts may still have 100 GB bandwidth and 300 build minutes.
notes: Excellent Git workflow, deploy previews, forms and serverless functions. New accounts are credit-based (since late 2025), so heavy traffic can exhaust the 300 credits quickly.

name: Vercel
limits: Hobby is for personal, non-commercial use only. 100 GB fast data transfer, 1M function invocations, 4 CPU-hours, 360 GB-hours memory, 100 deployments/day, 50 domains per project and 45-minute builds. Commercial use requires Pro.
notes: Great Next.js and frontend DX with previews, edge functions and analytics. The Hobby plan explicitly bans commercial projects; overages pause features until the cycle resets.

name: Render
limits: Free web services: 512 MB RAM, 0.1 CPU, spin down after 15 minutes idle, about 1 minute cold start, 750 instance hours/month. Static sites never sleep but share 5 GB bandwidth and 500 build minutes/month. Free Postgres expires after 30 days.
notes: One of the few free hosts that runs a real backend (Node, Python, Go, Rust, Docker). Free services are for testing and hobby use, not production.

name: Firebase Hosting
limits: Spark plan: 10 GB storage, 10 GB/month transfer with a hard 360 MB/day cap and a 2 GB max file. Exceeding quotas disables Hosting until the reset; Cloud Functions and Cloud Run require Blaze billing.
notes: Strong choice for Firebase apps: global CDN, preview channels, custom domains and SSL included. The daily transfer cap is the real limit for media-heavy sites.

name: Kinsta Static Site Hosting
limits: 600 build minutes/month per company, 1 concurrent build per site, 1 GB build image per site and 100 GB bandwidth/month. Static output only, with no server-side runtime.
notes: Premium-style static hosting on Cloudflare's network at no cost. Good for agencies with many small sites; overage is billed if you add a payment method.

name: Surge.sh
limits: Publishing is CLI-only. The free plan includes custom domains and managed SSL, but password protection, redirects, CORS and custom certificates are paid. No server-side code; fair-use limits apply.
notes: Fastest way to publish a static folder from the terminal. Great for demos and prototypes; there is no dashboard build pipeline.

name: Neocities
limits: Free accounts get 1 GB storage, 200 GB bandwidth/month and a neocities.org subdomain. Only allowlisted file types, one site per account, and custom domains need Supporter ($5/month).
notes: Ad-free, community-run host for hand-made personal sites. In-browser editor, CLI and RSS; custom domains and larger storage require Supporter.

name: tiiny.host
limits: Free plan: 3 MB uploads (0.5 MB for PDFs), one active project, and links are kept while you log in at least every 3 months. Custom domains require Solo ($13/month billed yearly).
notes: Drag-and-drop host for a single small HTML page or ZIP. Useful for quick demos, not for full sites or media.

name: InfinityFree
limits: 30,000 inode cap, 50,000 hits/day (every file request counts), no email, no SSH, no cron since 2023, forum-only support. Accounts with almost no visitors for 30 days can be deactivated.
notes: The most generous classic free host: PHP 8.3, MySQL 8, VistaPanel, Softaculous and free SSL. Inode and hit limits, not storage, usually break WordPress sites.

name: ByetHost
limits: 10 MB maximum upload. Free SSL is automatic on Byet subdomains; on your own domain you install a certificate yourself. Soft CPU/RAM limits apply. No card and no forced ads.
notes: Same iFastNet platform as InfinityFree, with unlimited databases and 5 GB NVMe. A good alternative when you need more databases; cron support is advertised but unreliable.

name: ProFreeHost
limits: iFastNet/VistaPanel platform with soft CPU and hit limits, 10 MB upload cap, no email, no SSH and no cron. Free SSL on subdomains; own-domain SSL may need manual setup.
notes: An InfinityFree-style clone. Features and limits are nearly identical; pick it only if InfinityFree signups are unavailable.

name: AwardSpace
limits: About 5,000 visits/month, 1 GB storage and 5 GB traffic. The free plan has no SSL Manager, so HTTPS needs a paid plan. cURL and socket functions are disabled, which breaks many WordPress plugins. Accounts can be deleted after 12 months without traffic.
notes: Long-running ad-free host with one mailbox and a CMS installer. Fine for a small static or PHP brochure site; not suitable for WordPress updates or API-heavy apps.

name: FreeHostia
limits: 250 MB disk, 6 GB/month traffic, 2 MB maximum file upload, 10 MB MySQL database, 3 mailboxes, no cron or SSH on free. Small WordPress installs hit the database cap quickly.
notes: Ad-free Chocolate plan with Let's Encrypt SSL and support for 5 domains. Best for tiny HTML/PHP sites or beginner experiments.

name: HelioHost
limits: Log in at least every 30 days or the account is suspended. Resource caps are 200 GB memory and 10,000 CPU units/day. Free Johnny signups are rationed (slots at 00:00 and 12:00 UTC); no SSH. One account per person.
notes: Non-profit host with Plesk, unlimited databases and email, and many runtimes (Node, Python, Java, .NET, Go, Ruby). The most developer-friendly free shared host, if you can get a slot.

name: GoogieHost
limits: 1 GB NVMe, free subdomain or custom domain, DirectAdmin, PHP 8, MySQL and free Let's Encrypt SSL. Unmetered traffic is subject to CPU/RAM fair use; the plan is sized for roughly 10,000 monthly visitors and exact resource caps are not published.
notes: No forced ads, free business email and Softaculous. A solid InfinityFree alternative with less storage but a simpler, ad-free DirectAdmin panel.

name: x10Hosting
limits: 500 MB initial web space, 3 domains, 3 email accounts, 2 MySQL databases, DirectAdmin and a 300+ app installer. Free signups are paused for maintenance as of October 2026; existing accounts continue. Resource limits apply and quota increases can be requested.
notes: Long-running free host since 2004 with a real control panel. The free tier is small but upgradeable; check whether signups have reopened before relying on it.

name: Serv00
limits: 512 MB RAM, 15 processes, 3 PHP interpreters, 3 TCP/UDP ports, 3 Git/SVN/Hg repositories and 7-day backups. FreeBSD shared host in the EU with forum-only support and no SLA. Signups open in limited batches.
notes: Unusually capable free shared host: SSH, cron, many runtimes, 100 sites and free SSL. Still not a VPS, so do not expect dedicated resources.

name: Alwaysdata
limits: Free plan: 1 GB disk (includes mail), 256 MB RAM and 1/4 CPU. Custom domains are no longer available on the free tier after the 2025 change, and commercial use is not allowed. SSH, FTP and WebDAV access included.
notes: Polished managed host with many runtimes and one-click installers. The free tier is a personal sandbox, not a custom-domain production host.

name: PythonAnywhere
database: SQLite; MySQL only on older free accounts
limits: Free Beginner plan: 1 web app at yourusername.pythonanywhere.com, 512 MB disk, 100 CPU-seconds/day and 2 consoles. No custom domain; unused free web apps expire after 1 month. New free accounts (since January 2026) have no MySQL or scheduled tasks, and accounts inactive for 6 months can be deleted.
notes: Best free option for Flask/Django demos and Python scripts. The CPU-second quota is tiny, so it suits low-traffic apps and learning, not production.

name: FreeHosting.com
limits: Free hosting requires a registered domain; free subdomains are not offered. SSL, cron, SSH, extra databases and app mail are one-time paid add-ons. PHP memory is 256 MB, uploads 200 MB and execution time 60 seconds. Not available in some countries.
notes: The largest free shared storage on this list (10 GB) with unmetered bandwidth and cPanel-style tools. SSL is not free, so budget for the add-on or put Cloudflare in front.

name: WebHostMost
limits: 125 MB NVMe, unlimited inodes and bandwidth, DirectAdmin, PHP up to 8.3, Node.js and free Let's Encrypt SSL. Free plan includes one parked domain, one database and one email account, with reduced performance, SMTP disabled and a monthly login requirement.
notes: No-ads, no-card free plan that supports both PHP and Node. Good for a tiny site or test project; too small for media-heavy WordPress.

name: WordPress.com
limits: Free plan: WordPress.com subdomain only, 1 GB storage, ads shown to visitors, no plugins, no premium themes, no custom domain and no monetization. Paid plans unlock a domain, more storage and plugins.
notes: Fastest way to start a hosted WordPress blog. The free tier is ad-supported and locked down; WordPress.org plus a free PHP host gives full control.

name: Wix
limits: Free plan: 500 MB storage, 1 GB bandwidth/month, a wixsite.com subdomain, mandatory Wix branding and ads, no custom domain, no Google Analytics and no ecommerce. Up to 999 free sites per account.
notes: Best drag-and-drop builder if you need a polished site fast and can live with Wix branding and a weak bandwidth cap. Content is not portable.

name: Weebly
limits: Free plan: 500 MB storage, unlimited bandwidth, 10 MB maximum file, Weebly/Square branding and ads, no custom domain, limited apps and themes. A basic store with up to 10 products is included.
notes: Simple drag-and-drop builder owned by Square. The free plan is ad-supported; good for a basic site or a tiny store test.

name: Google Sites
limits: New Google Sites content counts toward your Google Account's 15 GB free storage, shared with Drive, Gmail and Photos. Custom domains require Google Workspace; free sites live at sites.google.com/view/name. Very limited design, no server-side code and few SEO controls.
notes: Zero-cost, ad-free option for simple team, wiki or portfolio pages. Best when you already use Google Workspace or need a quick internal site.

name: Webflow
limits: Starter Site plan: 2 static pages, 1 GB bandwidth/month, 50 lifetime form submissions, 50 CMS items, a webflow.io subdomain only, Webflow badge and no custom code. Some features require a paid Site plan.
notes: Professional visual designer with clean markup, but the free tier is a demo: two pages, 1 GB traffic, no custom code and a permanent Webflow badge.
